Imaging Services | 15 January 2025 | Multiparametric Prostate MRI
Clinical Indication: Re-evaluation prompted by PSA reaching 9.1 ng/mL alongside a previously positive biopsy.

FINDINGS:
Prostatic parenchyma occupies 56.5 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a 14 mm focal hypointense focus within the right mid-gland peripheral zone. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction, mirrored by reduced ADC signal. Post-contrast phases demonstrate early, localized enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. Seminal vesicles appear intact. No extracapsular spread or suspicious lymph nodes are evident.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone.
PSA density: 0.161 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.0.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Routine wellness visit and PSA tracking conducted. Historical values show 5.4 ng/mL in March 2022, followed by 4.5 ng/mL in February 2023. Occasional urinary frequency is noted, though obstructive complaints remain absent. The upward PSA trend combined with the patient’s age prompted a urology referral for comprehensive assessment and imaging review.
